s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with epigastric tenderness and radiating back pain
salient_findings: Progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
key_facts: 60-year-old African American woman
One-day duration of symptoms
No history of fever, chills, or previous similar pain
No abdominal trauma or alcohol/illicit drug use
Medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease
Current medications include insulin, amlodipine, and aspirin
Vital signs: temperature 36.7 °C, blood pressure 200/100 mm Hg, heart rate 84 beats/min
Abdominal examination showed generalized tenderness worst in the epigastrium
Lipase level: 13.6833 µkat/L (elevated)
Triglycerides: 80 mg/dL (0.9 mmol/L)
No acute abnormality of the pancreas on computed helical tomography

shortlist.label: Acute Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated lipase level and epigastric tenderness

shortlist.label: Peptic Ulcer Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Epigastric pain and history of pantoprazole use

shortlist.label: Cholecystitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of cholecystectomy and abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Autoimmune Pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and elevated lipase level, with potential for autoimmune component

raw.rationale: Elevated lipase level and severe epigastric pain radiating to the back are key indicators of acute pancreatitis, despite the absence of acute abnormality on computed tomography, which can sometimes be seen in early stages of the disease.

rejected.label: Hypertriglyceridemia-induced Pancreatitis
rejected.why: Triglyceride level is within normal range, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Peptic Ulcer Disease
rejected.why: Patient used pantoprazole without relief and there's no specific indication of peptic ulcer disease in the provided information

rejected.label: Cholecystitis
rejected.why: Patient has a history of cholecystectomy, making cholecystitis impossible

rejected.label: Autoimmune Pancreatitis
rejected.why: There's no specific indication of autoimmune pancreatitis, such as elevated IgG4 levels or characteristic imaging findings, in the provided information
